items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: You wrote all these things for Art Neville. Right. Which, of course, did very well.

ctx.x: It does, it does. And not too long after that, I think it was in the late 60s, you all put together the meters. Were the meters together before they came to you all, or did you kind of connect them up?
No, they were together, very much so. Art Neville and the Neville Sound, playing at the Ivanhoe. A great little band. And that's how they came.
And the song that came out at that time, no, I'll wait a little bit on that. So then they came into the studio. Did you see them at that point as being a New Orleans answer to Booker T and the MGs?

items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: I didn't go in with them. By that time, I wasn't working with Aaron anymore. In fact, back during the days of Hercules is the last time I actually worked with Aaron.

ctx.x: I don't know. When we were through with it, I listened and it... It sounded like an awful lot of words, but I sort of liked it. It was written especially for Aaron to do. If it wasn't for Aaron, a song like that wouldn't have been written. To say those things. There are a lot of lines in there as the kind of lines that Aaron rapped when he talked. He talked like that. And he inspires a lot of things. Not that that's a different story that I know of, but... I could easily set up a scene from Aaron talk and write…

I played that song on a show we did with the Neville Brothers about two months ago. And I don't think it's possible to find a copy of that record anywhere in the city now. Because there's such a huge response to it. And when it came out, I never heard it here in New Orleans.

It didn't do much at all. And it was a different sounding record for us. It was a little more... It sounded like a little more percussion. A little more production also. But it didn't do very much, but we liked it.
